title: ISERROR vs ISERR vs ISNA: how wide a net
meta_desc: ISERROR vs ISERR vs ISNA compared: which errors each detects, the parallel with IFERROR/IFNA, and ERROR.TYPE for telling errors apart.
intro: Three error detectors that differ only in scope: ISERROR catches everything, ISNA catches only #N/A (the 'not found' signal), and ISERR is the odd middle child — everything EXCEPT #N/A. Same philosophy as IFERROR vs IFNA: match the net to what you actually expect.

cols: Real-bug detection while tolerating lookup misses

when.use_when: Around lookups — 'did we find it?' — leaving genuine formula bugs visible. The test half of what IFNA does in one step.
The audit trick: TRUE only for NON-lookup errors, so COUNTIF-style sweeps with ISERR find real breakage in a sheet full of expected #N/As.
Dashboards and validation columns where any failure should raise the same flag — accepting that it can't distinguish a miss from a bug.

compat_note: All four execute identically in every LibreOffice build and in the Google Sheets run we execute (Excel per Microsoft's docs — we do not run Excel). ERROR.TYPE is the escalation path when the boolean tests aren't enough — it returns a code per error kind (#N/A is 7), letting one formula branch differently on misses vs genuine faults.
